title: WireGuard preset binds lnd admin REST API to 0.0.0.0, protected by firewall only
description: When lndconnect is enabled with the wireguard preset, lnd's macaroon-admin REST API listens on all interfaces. Protection relies solely on nixos-fw default-drop plus an accept rule that is now correctly interface-pinned (`-i wg-nb`) and source-pinned to the single peer /32 (fixed in HEAD d22c5da). The rebind to the wg address is deliberately deferred because nbLib.address maps 0.0.0.0 -> 127.0.0.1 and all internal consumers depend on it.
impact: If the firewall is misconfigured or bypassed (e.g. user-added accept rules), the lnd admin REST API is network-reachable. TLS + admin macaroon still required, so this is defense-in-depth loss, not direct compromise.
remediation: Tracked with a full breakage checklist in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md. No action needed beyond the documented plan.

title: `+`-prefixed rootScript runs fully unsandboxed (bypasses ProtectSystem=strict), not just User=
description: Verified empirically on systemd: an ExecStartPost prefixed with `+` executes with no mount-namespace confinement at all (mkdir in /run outside RuntimeDirectory succeeds under ProtectSystem=strict). The lnd-create-macaroons script that depends on this is carefully hardened (root-only staging, atomic rename, de-privileged macaroon read, 64KiB cap, jq -e), so nothing is exploitable today. The risk is latent: any future rootScript addition inherits zero sandboxing, and the missing `set -u` in nbLib.script means a refactor that unsets $RUNTIME_DIRECTORY would redirect `mv` targets to the filesystem root as unsandboxed root.
impact: None today. Latent footgun: small edits to the macaroon script or RuntimeDirectory config could become root file-overwrite bugs.
remediation: Optional hardening: add `set -u` to nbLib.script and a guard like `[ -n "$RUNTIME_DIRECTORY" ] || exit 1` in the macaroon script.

title: bitcoind .cookie is group-readable, granting full privileged RPC to group bitcoin (operator)
description: postStart chmods the RPC cookie 0640 root-equivalent-readable by group bitcoin, which includes the operator. This equals full privileged bitcoind RPC (wallet, P2P control) for the operator. Documented in the code comment (audit L-10) with guidance to prefer rpc user + HMAC for new services.
impact: Operator (already funds-equivalent via `doas -u lnd` seed access) gets full bitcoind RPC. Consistent with the fork's operator-is-admin trust model.
remediation: None required; keep new consumers on rpc users + HMAC as the comment states.

title: Operator is funds-equivalent by design (nopass doas to lnd, netns-exec cap_sys_admin)
description: secure-node grants the operator nopass `doas -u lnd` (can read the 0400 lnd-seed-mnemonic) and ownership of the cap_sys_admin netns-exec wrapper. These are deliberate convenience boundaries; the threat model treats the operator as trusted. Worth restating because it means 'service isolation' on this fork does not extend to the operator account.
impact: Compromise of the operator SSH key is full node compromise. Expected by design, but users should protect that key accordingly.
remediation: Document explicitly in docs/security posture if not already; no code change.

title: nix-bitcoin-wg-connect host autodetection queries third-party IP-echo services
description: Running nix-bitcoin-wg-connect without a host argument shells out to lndconnect's external-IP discovery (go-external-ip), which contacts external providers and reveals the node's IP to them. Noted in the code comment.
impact: Privacy leak of the node's IP to third-party echo services during QR pairing.
remediation: Pass the host explicitly (`nix-bitcoin-wg-connect <host>`) to skip autodetection.

title: Committed SSH private key in examples/qemu-vm
description: A world-known private key authorized for root/operator in the QEMU demo VM configs. Both deploy-qemu-vm.sh and deploy-krops.sh carry a prominent 'MAKE SURE TO REPLACE the SSH identity file' warning, and the key is only referenced by example code.
impact: Only if a user copies the example verbatim into a real deployment.
remediation: None; warnings are adequate for example material.

title: cve-scan.sh summary text contradicts scan target
description: The generated triage note says 'whitelist test/build tooling (this scans the full test closure)' while the script header and scan target are the node RUNTIME closure (scan-node.nix). Cosmetic, but it misleads future triagers about what the whitelist covers.
impact: None on security posture; possible triage confusion.
remediation: Drop 'test closure' wording from the summary hint.

title: Weekly CVE scan does not scan the recommended deployment: tor, duplicity and the secure-node preset are absent from the scan target
description: scan-node.nix enables only bitcoind, lnd, electrs, btcpayserver/nbxplorer with generateSecrets. It does not import the secure-node/enable-tor presets, so the scanned runtime closure contains no tor, no duplicity (services.backups), and none of the preset infrastructure. The README and cve-scan.sh sell the scan as covering 'the shipped closure ... the software a user actually runs'. On the recommended deployment, tor is the component with the largest continuously-exposed internet parsing surface (client + onion services on every secure-node node).
impact: A CVE in tor (or duplicity) that is unfixed in the pinned nixpkgs is never reported by the weekly scan, and the fork's stated remediation path for scan findings (version-guarded overrides in pkgs/overrides.nix) can never trigger for it. The control silently under-covers the highest-exposure component, which is the same failure class as the fail-open bugs fixed in 1caa0af.
recommendation: Import modules/presets/secure-node.nix (or at minimum enable services.tor + services.backups) in scan-node.nix, then re-baseline .github/cve-whitelist.toml. Secondary note: the whitelist's blanket build-tool pname entries (gcc, go, cargo, ...) should carry the nixpkgs rev they were triaged against, since blanket pnames stay silent across pin moves.

title: lnd REST (admin-macaroon API) bound to 0.0.0.0 in the wireguard preset, protected by the host firewall alone
description: When lndconnect is enabled, the preset sets services.lnd.restAddress = "0.0.0.0", so the REST API that the admin macaroon authenticates listens on every interface. Exposure is prevented only by nixos-fw default-drop plus the accept rule, which since HEAD is correctly scoped to '-i wg-nb -s <peerAddress>/32', plus the restrictPeer REJECT rules. The bind itself remains deferred with a thorough breakage checklist (cert SANs, lnd-wg startup coupling, macaroon ExecStartPost, btcpayserver backend, lndconnect onion target). Note also lndconnect-wg passes --nocert (upstream-inherited), so Zeus users accept a cert warning against the wg address.
impact: Any firewall regression (rule ordering, an interface rename, a future preset refactor) silently exposes a wallet-admin API on all interfaces. Current compensating controls make practical exploitation require a spoofed wg peer or a firewall bug.
recommendation: Ship the deferral doc's own recommended design: keep restAddress at 127.0.0.1 and add a second listener via services.lnd.extraConfig 'restlisten=<serverAddress>:<port>' plus the lnd-wants-wireguard ordering and the doc's pre-flight checklist. That variant avoids all six documented breakages.

title: Documented krops install/update flow is dead post-guard, and its only signposted exit deploys unpatched archived upstream
location: docs/install.md:226 (§3.3 'Obtain the hash of the latest nix-bitcoin release'); docs/configuration.md:14-18 ('Updating nix-bitcoin' / update-nix-bitcoin); examples/importable-configuration.nix:8-12; helper/makeShell.nix:65-77 (update-nix-bitcoin -> fetch-release)
description: Since c3253f3, helper/fetch-release exits 1 for this fork unless NIX_BITCOIN_FETCH_UPSTREAM is set. But the primary non-flake install path (install.md krops tutorial), the documented update command (update-nix-bitcoin in the deployment shell), and the importable-configuration example still route users through fetch-release. The refusal message's only actionable override fetches fort-nix/nix-bitcoin releases, which contain none of this fork's fixes (the exact outcome the guard exists to prevent).
impact: As shipped it fails closed (users hit an error), but every krops user following the docs reaches a dead end whose only signposted workaround silently drops all fork security fixes, including the ones behind the fork's existence. f51bd87 fixed the flake examples but left the non-flake flow stale.
recommendation: Rewrite install.md §3.3, configuration.md's update section, and importable-configuration.nix around a fork-native pin (e.g. builtins.fetchTarball of a pinned commit of ostermayer/nix-bitcoin, or a flake-ref krops source). If the upstream escape hatch stays, have it emit a loud 'UNPATCHED UPSTREAM, NOT THIS FORK' marker into the generated nix-bitcoin-release.nix.
file: docs/install.md:226 (§3.3 'Obtain the hash of the latest nix-bitcoin release'); docs/configuration.md:14-18 ('Updating nix-bitcoin' / update-nix-bitcoin); examples/importable-configuration.nix:8-12; helper/makeShell.nix:65-77 (update-nix-bitcoin -> fetch-release)

title: Release tags are unsigned, contradicting SECURITY.md's signing claim
location: .github/workflows/release-tag.yml (git tag -a, bot identity, no signing key); SECURITY.md ('Commits and tags on this fork are signed with the maintainer's SSH key')
description: Commits are genuinely SSH-signed (verified on d22c5da). But the CalVer release tags users are told to pin by name are created by CI with 'git tag -a' and a github-actions bot identity, i.e. unsigned. git verify-tag on any release tag fails.
impact: Users who follow SECURITY.md's verification guidance for the most trust-critical refs (release snapshots) get a failing check with no explanation. Flake pinners remain protected by flake.lock narHash regardless.
recommendation: Either sign tags in the release job (tag -s with a protected key, or move tagging to a maintainer-side signed step), or narrow the SECURITY.md claim to commits and manually created tags.
file: .github/workflows/release-tag.yml (git tag -a, bot identity, no signing key); SECURITY.md ('Commits and tags on this fork are signed with the maintainer's SSH key')

title: setup-secrets: root service handling the entire secrets dir with zero systemd sandboxing
status: open (upstream parity, not a fork regression)
description: setup-secrets runs as root with no ProtectSystem, PrivateTmp, NoNewPrivileges, RestrictAddressFamilies, or capability bounding, while performing globbing, chown/chmod, and secret generation (openssl, pwgen, python) over the node's most sensitive directory. Its sibling root service onion-addresses received defaultHardening, PrivateNetwork, and a minimal capability set during the fork's hardening rounds; setup-secrets is now the least-confined root service in the fork.
impact: A future bug in this script (or in the generated-secrets tooling it runs) has unconfined root reach. No current exploit path found; the script's own logic is careful (symlink-unsafe operations are all on root-controlled paths).
recommendation: Apply a scoped sandbox: ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=<secretsDir>, PrivateTmp, NoNewPrivileges, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX, CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_CHOWN CAP_FOWNER CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE (CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH only if the manual-setup path requires reading foreign files).

title: btcpayserver/nbxplorer rely on the NixOS default postgres HBA; the shared unix socket is the real (and netns-invisible) cross-service boundary
status: open (inherited from upstream module; depends on pinned nixpkgs default)
location: modules/btcpayserver.nix:126-145 (services.postgresql: ensureDatabases/ensureUsers + ALTER DATABASE OWNER; no explicit services.postgresql.authentication)
description: nbxplorer and btcpayserver connect via the /run/postgresql unix socket. Unix-domain sockets are not isolated by netns-isolation, so for these two services the postgres HBA is the actual service-isolation boundary. The module sets no authentication policy and inherits whatever the pinned nixpkgs postgresql module defaults to for local socket auth. If that default is (or becomes) weaker than peer auth for the relevant roles, any local compromised service user can connect as btcpayserver/nbxplorer and fully administer btcpaydb and the nbxplorer DB (invoice/store data, derived-address metadata).
impact: Uncertain by construction (it is a distro-default dependency): either a non-issue under peer auth, or a quiet collapse of the claimed service-isolation boundary at the DB layer. Could not be verified offline against the pinned nixpkgs revs (93108a5 / 422d1ae).
recommendation: Set services.postgresql.authentication explicitly in the module (peer for local unix-socket connections, or scram for anything else) so the boundary does not track nixpkgs defaults across weekly pin moves; verify the generated pg_hba.conf in the VM test.
file: modules/btcpayserver.nix:126-145 (services.postgresql: ensureDatabases/ensureUsers + ALTER DATABASE OWNER; no explicit services.postgresql.authentication)

title: tests.py retains dead branches for services removed by the trim
location: test/tests.py (netns-isolation: clightning/liquidd/rtl/lightning-loop reachability lists; backups: clightning/joinmarket file list; regtest: fulcrum/clightning/lightning-loop/lightning-pool/mempool blocks; joinmarket capsh check)
description: Multiple test branches reference removed services. They are unreachable (enabled_tests can never contain them), and the netns test's 'nb-clightning is not an allowed netns' assertion now passes for a different reason than it was written for (the netns no longer exists at all, and netns-exec's whitelist also rejects it).
impact: No security impact; misleads future readers about what is covered and can mask a re-introduction error.
recommendation: Delete the dead branches; keep one explicit assertion that trimmed-service netns names are rejected by netns-exec (which is the actual invariant).
file: test/tests.py (netns-isolation: clightning/liquidd/rtl/lightning-loop reachability lists; backups: clightning/joinmarket file list; regtest: fulcrum/clightning/lightning-loop/lightning-pool/mempool blocks; joinmarket capsh check)
